The Strategy Manager serves as a strategic advisor, business finance partner, and execution partner to the Chief Administrative Officer of HCPD. The position increases the CAO’s executive capacity by translating complex enterprise and departmental priorities into clearly defined strategies, financially substantiated business plans, coordinated initiatives, accountable implementation plans, and measurable results.

Working horizontally across HCPD’s leadership structure, the Strategy Manager leads or coordinates priorities that cross functional boundaries, involve Health System and Campus partners, require executive level analysis, or do not reside fully within a single director’s portfolio. The Strategy Manager integrates their contributions, strengthens the strategic and financial case for their priorities, and helps align their work with the direction of the CAO and the broader enterprise.

A major focus of the role is developing and advancing enterprise business plans and value improvement initiatives. These efforts may involve cost savings, cost avoidance, revenue enhancement, procurement and contract optimization, operational efficiency, shared services, regulatory risk reduction, improved resource utilization, infrastructure planning, and other opportunities that create measurable organizational value.

The position provides executive strategy, analysis, and follow through support to the CAO by preparing decision ready information, maintaining visibility into strategic commitments, identifying emerging risks, coordinating cross functional actions, and determining when executive intervention is required.
Demonstrated discretion and sound judgment when handling confidential, sensitive, or politically complex matters.
Advanced knowledge of organizational strategy, strategic planning, business planning, performance management, organizational effectiveness, and complex initiative execution.
Familiarity with University of California structures, policies, financial processes, capital programs, or Health and Campus relationships.
Demonstrated ability to identify root causes, develop practical recommendations, establish performance measures, and support sustained implementation.
Knowledge of organizational effectiveness, operating model design, process improvement, change management, or related practices.
Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex, incomplete, or inconsistent information into concise, accurate, and decision ready recommendations.
Knowledge of project and program management methodologies, Lean Six Sigma, structured problem solving, and organizational change implementation.
Strong facilitation, negotiation, stakeholder management, and conflict resolution skills.
Ability to establish accountability, manage competing priorities, and maintain momentum across organizational boundaries.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with executive, operational, financial, technical, and external audiences.
